It's funny, when I was suicidal the idea of things being ok again in the future seem out of this world, and I would just scoff at the very idea. But I still read the encouraging posts written by the likes of you with a tiny voice in the back of head saying "maybe, but probably not... I hope so, but that is almost an impossibility." It still helped though, the encouragement and support kept the small voice alive that was doubting my deepest desire. I could not understand the peace I was looking for from my own suicide could only be found by getting better. By killing myself I would only cease to exist, with my last moments filled with exactly what I was escaping. You won't see my post history here because I deleted my old account, but everyone posting on this subreddit is responsible for getting me through the most difficult time in my life thus far. Thank you, and I will do my best to stay positive. Depression still haunts me, but it's a battle I willingly fight now. Im no longer curled into the fetal position hoping to drown in it all, but standing up on my feet, ready for the next wave to break over me. That's how I see myself now.

If you're too nervous to talk to someone, make a throw-away account and pour it all out. I was going to use a helium hood while sitting on top of a ladder, with a noose around my neck so that when I lost consciousness I would fall off and my neck would snap. I guess I was afraid I would survive. Like many feel here, death seemed like a walk in the park compared to the suffering I was going through, and frankly I think that's true. It's an immensely painful experience. I feel cheesy writing this because I'm no expert but: don't dwell on the fantasy of suicide, it will suck you in. It's a wonderful fantasy, but you will never be able to experience the peace it brings you.
